name: Upright row
pattern: Vertical pull close to the body: elbows lift out and up to shoulder height while the hands stay near the trunk.
setup: Stand tall, bar in front of your thighs, overhand grip.
Hands about shoulder width or wider, not touching.
Brace, shoulders down, look straight ahead.

steps.text: Lift your elbows out and up, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height, bar around the lower chest.

cues.cue: Elbows to shoulder height, not higher.
cues.why: The arm is turned in during this lift; above about 90° that pinches the rotator cuff under the shoulder bone.
Wider grips raise deltoid and trapezius activity and lower biceps work.

cues.cue: Lead with the elbows, elbows above the wrists.
cues.why: Pulling with the elbows keeps the load on the shoulders, not the forearms.

cues.cue: Bar close to your body the whole time.
cues.why: A bar drifting forward adds strain on the lower back and front shoulder.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Controlled; brief hold at the top.

mistakes.name: Elbows too high
mistakes.looks: Elbows go well above the shoulders and the bar reaches the chin.
mistakes.why: Raising the turned-in arm past 90° is the impingement position.

mistakes.name: Hands too close
mistakes.looks: Hands touching in the middle of the bar.
mistakes.fix: Move hands to shoulder width or wider.
mistakes.why: More internal rotation and more biceps, less deltoid.

mistakes.name: Body swing
mistakes.looks: Hips drive and the trunk leans back to lift the bar.
mistakes.why: Momentum replaces shoulder work and loads the lower back.

safety: Shoulder pain or impingement history: stop lower than it hurts, or replace with a lateral raise.
Wrist pain: use a wider grip, dumbbells, cable rope or straps.

variants.change: Wide grip (about 2x shoulder width): most deltoid and trap, least biceps.
Dumbbells: each hand finds its own path, often easier on the wrists and shoulders.
One arm: keep the trunk square.
Lying cable row: on your back pulling from a low pulley toward the head; same arm path.

motion.basis: Elevation limit and the internally rotated arm from schoenfeld2011; grip effects from mcallister2013 (50%, 100% and 200% of shoulder width tested). Joint angles are estimates: internal rotation of about 50° at the top follows from the elbows above the hands with the arm at 80°; scapular upward rotation scaled from mcclure2001; scapular elevation at the top reflects the upper-trap work (estimate).

sources.cite: Schoenfeld B, Kolber MJ, Haimes JE. The upright row: implications for preventing subacromial impingement. Strength Cond J. 2011;33(5):25-28.
McAllister MJ, Schilling BK, Hammond KG, Weiss LW, Farney TM. Effect of grip width on electromyographic activity during the upright row. J Strength Cond Res. 2013;27(1):181-187.
McClure PW, Michener LA, Sennett BJ, Karduna AR. Direct 3-dimensional measurement of scapular kinematics during dynamic movements in vivo. J Shoulder Elbow Surg. 2001;10(3):269-277.
Haff GG, Triplett NT, eds. Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning. 4th ed. National Strength and Conditioning Association. Human Kinetics; 2016.
